title: Copy
purpose: When an ad, page, email or listing is about to ship or has stopped selling, open Copy to get words that are true, match the page and sell, without rewriting them myself at night.
fires: the founder's late-night rewrite, the freelancer's unchecked drafts, the doc of old headlines, and finding out about a bad claim from a rejection email
not_for: a store with no live ads, pages or emails yet, or a brand looking for a new brand idea or a naming agency's full service

jobs.job: When our best ad is getting more expensive and the media buyer needs new words by Friday, give me copy built from what buyers say that wins on cost per purchase, not on clicks, so I launch fresh ads without paying more for each sale
jobs.circumstance: Wednesday, cost per purchase on the top ad up 25 percent in 2 weeks, a launch slot booked for Friday, the media buyer waiting on copy

progress.functional: get 3 to 5 copy sets that bring buyers at or under the target cost per purchase
progress.emotional: stop hoping the freelancer's lines work; feel the next launch is in safe hands
progress.social: hand the media buyer copy they trust, and not be the founder who holds up the launch

jobs.hire_today: a freelance copywriter, the agency's creative team, or the founder writing at night
jobs.fire: the freelancer's untested drafts and the late-night rewrite; the habit of picking lines by click rate

forces.push: every week without fresh copy the top ad gets more expensive
forces.pull: copy sets ranked by how they are likely to do on cost per purchase, in the buyer's own words
forces.habit: the same freelancer has always written the ads
forces.anxiety: what if the new lines lose to the old ones and I wasted a week of spend

jobs.little_hire: every launch slot, and any week the top ad's cost per purchase rises 15 percent or more

watch.metric: cost per purchase by copy set, 7 day click, first 14 days live

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the 3 newest copy sets cost $41 per purchase against a $32 target. After: new sets land at $31 within 14 days of launch.
jobs.not_for: a store with no live ads, or one spending under $1,000 a month, where one good set a quarter is enough

jobs.job: When new ads are due to go live tomorrow and I do not know if a line breaks Meta's rules or promises something we cannot back, check every claim, review quote and guarantee first, so I launch without a rejection or a promise we cannot keep
jobs.circumstance: the night before a launch, 20 ads drafted, no one has checked the claims, the account had a warning last quarter

progress.functional: know which lines are banned, unproven or wrong on the guarantee, and get a fix for each
progress.emotional: stop lying awake about an account ban; feel safe pressing launch
progress.social: show a partner or client that nothing risky goes out under the brand's name

jobs.hire_today: nothing, or the founder reading drafts at speed; most learn only when an ad is rejected
jobs.fire: the quick read before launch and the habit of finding out from a rejection email

forces.push: one rejected ad can pause delivery and one false claim can bring a complaint
forces.pull: every line marked pass, fix or block, with the proof behind each pass
forces.habit: we have always shipped and fixed rejections after
forces.anxiety: what if the check blocks a line that was fine and slows every launch

jobs.little_hire: before every launch, and whenever a new claim or guarantee is written

watch.metric: ads rejected for policy, trailing 30 days

drives.metric: days of lost delivery from rejections and account warnings, trailing 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6 ads rejected in 30 days and 1 account warning. After: 0 rejections from claims in the next 30 days, every claim with proof on file.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no claims beyond price and colour, where a quick read is enough

jobs.job: When people visit a product page but do not buy and I do not know which doubt stops them, find the doubt that costs the most sales and give me the line that answers it, so I fix the one thing that is holding sales back
jobs.circumstance: end of month, a product with good traffic and a weak add to cart rate, reviews and tickets unread, a copywriter guessing

progress.functional: know the top objection from reviews and tickets and have a line for it in the ad and on the page
progress.emotional: stop guessing why people do not buy
progress.social: show the team the reason comes from buyers, not from the founder's taste

jobs.hire_today: nothing; the copywriter answers the doubts they imagine, and reviews and tickets go unread for this
jobs.fire: writing from the founder's opinion; the FAQ nobody reads

forces.push: traffic is paid for and leaves over the same doubt every day
forces.pull: objections ranked by how often buyers raise them, each with a line and a place to put it
forces.habit: we write what we think is great about the product
forces.anxiety: what if the top complaint is about the product itself and copy cannot fix it

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and whenever a product's add to cart rate falls 20 percent

watch.metric: product page conversion rate on pages with the new objection line, trailing 14 days

drives.metric: revenue per product page session, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1.4 percent of visitors buy and fit doubts sit in 30 percent of tickets. After: 1.8 percent within 21 days of adding a fit line.
jobs.not_for: a product with under 50 reviews and tickets, where there is not yet enough buyer voice to rank doubts

jobs.job: When a proven ad starts to cost 30 percent more per sale and the buyer wants to kill it or cut the price, tell me whether to change the headline, the price line or the offer first, so I save the ad without giving away margin

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer killing the ad or asking for a discount
jobs.fire: the reflex to discount or kill a winner

forces.push: a winner is fading and a discount would cost margin on every order
forces.pull: a headline-first rewrite with the price and offer left alone unless the headline fails
forces.habit: when an ad fades, we kill it and move on
forces.anxiety: what if the new headline loses the buyers the old one found

jobs.little_hire: whenever a top 5 ad's cost per purchase rises 20 percent over 14 days

watch.metric: cost per purchase on the rewritten ad against the 14 days before, 7 day click

drives.metric: gross profit per ad dollar, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the old winner costs $44 a sale and the plan is 20 percent off. After: a new headline brings it to $34 with full price kept.
jobs.not_for: an ad that has run under 7 days or under 3 times the target cost per purchase; it has not failed yet

watch.metric: live ads whose headline, price or offer does not appear on their landing page

drives.metric: bounce rate of paid sessions on those pages, trailing 7 days

watch.metric: hours from rejection to the fixed ad spending again

drives.metric: days of lost delivery from rejections, trailing 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: rejected ads take 3 days to get back live. After: fixed and back live the same day.
jobs.not_for: a brand whose rejections come from the product category itself, which needs a policy lawyer, not new words

jobs.hire_today: nothing; nobody checks, the brand finds out from angry buyers

forces.push: every hour a dead offer stays live makes angry buyers and refunds
forces.pull: one list of stale lines across ads, flows and pages the moment the store changes

forces.anxiety: what if pulling a line pauses an ad that was still selling

watch.metric: live ads, emails and pages with a price, stock or deadline that no longer matches the store, checked daily

drives.metric: support tickets about a price or offer that did not apply, trailing 30 days
